key_insight: EchoLens localized fine-grained cardiac structures at expert-comparable reliability, while tested general-purpose and medical vision-language models and an open-vocabulary detector recalled 3% or fewer.
clinical_relevance: Explicit structure localization could help ground echocardiography AI outputs in visible anatomy, though clinical benefit remains unproven.
method: Trained a detector on 5,912 expert-annotated structures and 4,219 Doppler signals from 136 patients.
Covered 21 cardiac structures across 11 transthoracic views and 11 spectral Doppler signal types.
Evaluated against a blinded expert reader and physician review of external data.
evidence_signal: EchoLens recalled 87% of structures; box centers fell within reference regions in 95.7% of cases versus 95.3% for an expert, while external review judged 81–92% of detections correct and Doppler type identification reached 83%.
watch_item: The modest training cohort and localization-focused evaluation leave broader generalizability and downstream clinical impact to be established.
paper_title: Expert-level localization of fine-grained cardiac structures across the transthoracic echocardiogram
